## My Thinking

My family has farmed this land in Quzhou my whole life. I know this soil and this climate. The wheat-maize rotation is what I do, what my neighbors do, what makes sense here. The North China Plain grows these two crops — one in the ground all winter into June, then maize straight after until October. I have about 8 mu total. At 62, I can still manage that, though my back gives me trouble during harvest. My son is in Shijiazhuang and comes back for major busy periods if I need him.

I'll keep 7.5 mu in the wheat-maize rotation and about 0.5 mu near the house for vegetables — beans, eggplant, some greens — that's for eating and giving to neighbors, not really for selling.

For wheat I'll use the improved variety seeds from the township seed shop — probably Kenong 199 or whatever they have in stock. Not traditional seeds, those give lower yields. I'll do base fertilizer when I plant: compound fertilizer worked in, then top-dress urea at jointing. Three waterings: one before the ground freezes, one at jointing, one at heading. Last year the aphids were bad so I'll spray twice. I'll rotary till after the maize is harvested to prepare the seedbed.

For maize I buy hybrid seed, I have for years now. Zhengdan 958 is reliable. I plant it straight into the wheat stubble — no need to till again, saves me labor and diesel money. Summer rainfall here is usually decent but I'll water twice to be safe during the dry spells in August. Two pesticide passes for corn borer and earworm.

I won't try cotton. Too much handwork picking. I'm not young anymore.
